On behalf of Colorado River Alliance Intervenors - May 22,2026
  1                                       I.       INTRODUCTION

 2   Q.      PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND BUSINESS ADDRESS.

 3   A.               My name is Jason Buntz. My business address is 1504 W. 5th

 4           Street, Austin, Texas 78703.

 5   Q.      BY WHOM ARE YOU EMPLOYED AND IN WHAT CAPACITY?

 6   A.               I   am     the     Operations       Manager       for   Hicks   &   Company,

 7           Environmental/Archeological Consultants in Austin, Texas. I also serve as

 8           Program       Manager for the Environmental Compliance Management

 9           Program for the company.

10   Q.      ARE YOU           THE SAME JASON                  E.     BUNTZ WHO       PREVIOUSLY

11           SUBMITTED DIRECT TESTIMONY IN THIS PROCEEDING ON BEHALF

12           OF THE COLORADO RIVER ALLIANCE INTERVENORS?

13   A.               Yes.

14   Q.      DO YOU          INCORPORATE YOUR DIRECT TESTIMONY IN THIS

15           PROCEEDING INTO YOUR CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY?

16   A.               Yes.

17   Q.      WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY?

18   A.               My cross-rebuttal testimony addresses issues raised by the direct

19           testimony of Mr. Aaron Brewer, filed on behalf of Save the Lampasas,

20           Carpenter Land & Cattle, Martin, and the N3 Opposition Landowner

21           Group; and the direct testimony of Ms. Rae Lynn Schneider Reinecke,

22           filed on behalf of The Segment K13/K51 Landowners; Cherokee Creek

23           Partners; and Bonnie Helene McAnelly Individually, and as Trustee of The


     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349 and PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                                               Page 4
     Cross-rebuttal Testimony of Jason E. Buntz
     On behalf of Colorado River Alliance Intervenors - May 22,2026
  1           2025 Homestead Trust and The Bonnie Helene McAnelly 2023 Trust.

 2           Generally, with respect to the testimony of Mr. Brewer, I will address the

 3           comparison        of   Route      894,     the   "best-meets"   route   presented   by

 4           Oncor/LCRA TSC in the Application, with Route 572, one of several

 5           Alternative Routes identified by Mr. Brewer as being "superior" to Route

 6           894. Generally, with respect to the testimony of Ms. Reinecke, I will

 7           address the comparison of her proposed route "CCG" and her belief that

 8           Link J31 is the "superior option" for an Alternative Route proposed in this

 9           docket to cross the Colorado River.

10    Q.     DOES THE FACT THAT YOU ARE NOT ADDRESSING EVERY

11           OPINION         EXPRESSED             BY      THESE      AND     OTHER      PARTIES

12           CONSTITUTE AN ENDORSEMENT OF THEIR RECOMMENDATIONS?

13   A.               No, it does not.

14   Q.      WHICH ROUTE AMONG THE ALTERNATIVE ROUTES PROPOSED IN

15           THE APPLICATION                DID YOU           RECOMMEND IN YOUR DIRECT

16           TESTIMONY AS BEST MEETING THE CRITERIA UNDER PURA §

17           37.056(c) AND PUC SUBST. R. § 25.101(b)(3)(B)?

18   A.               In my direct testimony, I recommend that Route 894 be approved

19           as best meeting the Commission's criteria.

20                           Il.      RESPONSE TO AARON BREWER

21   Q.      HAVE YOU REVIEWED THE DIRECT TESTIMONY SUBMITTED IN

22           THIS DOCKET BY AARON BREWER ON BEHALF OF SAVE THE




     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349 and PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                                                Page 5
     Cross-rebuttal Testimony of Jason E. Buntz
     On behalf of Colorado River Alliance Intervenors - May 22,2026
  1           LAM PASAS, CARPENTER LAND & CATTLE, MARTIN, AND THE N3

 2           OPPOSITION LANDOWNER GROUP?

 3   A.               Yes, I have.

 4   Q.      WHICH STATEMENTS BY MR. BREWER IN PARTICULAR ARE YOU

 5           ADDRESSING IN THIS CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY?

 6   A.               I am addressing: 1) the statements by Mr. Brewer referring to

 7           individual Alternative Route Links proposed by the Applicants that "fail to

 8           meet the routing criteria in the Substantive Rule and other criteria in

 9           PURA" and 2) the statement on page 26 of Mr. Brewer's direct testimony

10           that the EA "understates Route 894's true [Endangered Species Act]

11           exposure.
12   Q.      COULD YOU DESCRIBE YOUR VIEW OF THE ARGUMENT MR.

13           BREWER           APPEARS            TO      MAKE         REGARDING      INDIVIDUAL

14           ALTERNATIVE             ROUTE         LINKS       THAT     FAI L   TO   MEET   THE

15           COMMISSION'S ROUTING CRITERIA?

16   A.               Yes. The Applicants are tasked by the Commission with routing

17           proposed transmission lines from endpoint to endpoint according to the

18           criteria in PURA and the Substantive Rule. Expecting Applicants to meet

19           these criteria for each and every link along a proposed route is

20           implausible, in my view. Evaluating any particular Alternative Route on the

21           basis of whether it has a single link or link combination that, for example,

22           does not parallel existing compatible rights of way, would seem to render

23           a conclusion that no route is prudent.


     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349 and PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                                            Page 6
     Cross-rebuttal Testimony of Jason E. Buntz
     On behalf of Colorado River Alliance Intervenors - May 22,2026
  1                    The fact that some links in an end-to-end transmission line route

 2           that is more than 200 miles long will have an effect on community values,

 3           aesthetics, cultural resources, or environmental integrity is self-evident. A

 4           determination of the extent to which an Alternative Route addresses the

 5           Commission's routing criteria can only be accomplished by an evaluation

 6           of the route from endpoint to endpoint. Choosing the Alternative Route

 7           that "best meets" the Commission's criteria, likewise, must take into

 8           account the overall effects of the route, including all of the links in that

 9           route.

10   Q.      MR. BREWER CITES THE CONSIDERATION OF GOLDEN-CHEEKED

11           WARBLER HABITAT AS A LIMITATION OF THE EA METHODOLOGY

12           EMPLOYED BY THE APPLICANTS. DO YOU AGREE WITH MR.

13           BREWER'S OPINION IN THIS SPECIFIC REGARD?

14   A.               I do, completely. In Table 7-2 in Appendix E of the EA, the

15           measurement of length of miles across known habitat of federally listed

16           endangered or threatened species is in truth a measurement of length of

17           miles across critical habitat as reflected in the Federal Registerl not as a

18           result of surveys or actual identification of habitat by the Applicants. Mr.

19           Brewer rightly points out that the United States Fish & Wildlife Service has

20           not designated critical habitat for the Golden-cheeked Warbler, and the EA

21           assumes, therefore, that habitat for this federally endangered species is

22           not known in the sense that it cannot be definitively quantified. The

23           Applicants do know where some habitat for the Golden-cheeked Warbler


     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349 and PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                                       Page 7
     Cross-rebuttal Testimony of Jason E. Buntz
     On behalf of Colorado River Alliance Intervenors - May 22,2026
  1           has been documented, though, as they indicate on Figure 3-7B in the EA

 2           that Colorado Bend State Park is known to include habitat for this federally

 3           endangered species.

 4                      Where I differ with Mr. Brewer's assessment, however, is in his

 5           assertion that Alternative Route 894 would somehow have a greater

 6           "exposure" to the Endangered Species Act than Route 572, the route that

 7           Mr. Brewer recommends that the Commission approve. Mr. Brewer cites

 8           Links G51-G52, which are part of Route 894, as being routed through an

 9           area of "confirmed" Golden-cheeked Warbler habitat and recommends

10           Route 572 instead. The problem with Mr. Brewer's recommendation,

11           though, is that Route 572 uses Link J31, which also passes through

12           Golden-cheeked Warbler habitat, as confirmed through Dr. Morrison's

13           direct testimony on behalf of the Colorado River Alliance Intervenors,

14           where his field survey detected the presence of Golden-cheeked Warblers

15           in habitat that would be eliminated by any route built in part using Link

16           J31.       Mr.    Brewer's suggestion,         if correct,   therefore,   that the   EA

17           methodology "understates Route 894's true [Endangered Species Act]

18           exposure" must then also apply to Route 572.

19               Ill.         RESPONSE TO RAE LYNN SCHNEIDER REINECKE

20   Q.      HAVE YOU REVIEWED THE DIRECT TESTIMONY SUBMITTED IN

21           THIS DOCKET BY RAE LYNN SCHNEIDER REINECKE ON BEHALF

22           OF THE SEGMENT K13/K51 LAN DOWNERS; CHEROKEE CREEK

23           PARTNERS; AND BONNIE HELENE MCANELLY INDIVIDUALLY, AND


     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349 and PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                                                 Page 8
     Cross-rebuttal Testimony of Jason E. Buntz
     On behalf of Colorado River Alliance Intervenors - May 22,2026
  1           AS TRUSTEE OF THE 2025 HOMESTEAD TRUST AND THE BONNIE

 2           HELENE MCANELLY 2023 TRUST?

 3   A.               Yes, I have.

 4   Q.      WHICH STATEMENTS BY MS. REINECKE IN PARTICULAR ARE YOU

 5           ADDRESSING IN THIS CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY?

 6   A.               I am addressing: 1) the statements by Ms. Reinecke favoring her

 7           proposed Route "CCG" over the Applicant's best meets route, Alternative

 8           Route 894; and 2) Ms. Reinecke's opinion that Link J31 is a "superior

 9           option" for crossing the Colorado River.

10   Q.      YOU REFERENCE A ROUTE THAT MS. REINECKE CALLS ROUTE

11           "CCG" IN HER DIRECT TESTIMONY. HAVE THE APPLICANTS

12           EVALUATED ROUTE "CCG"?

13   A.               Yes, in response to an RFI seeking information on an unfiled route

14           called "Cherokee Creek G."

15   Q.      HAVE YOU EVALUATED ROUTE "CCG"?

16   A.               Yes. As part of my review of Ms. Reinecke's direct testimony, I

17           evaluated her proposed Route "CCG".

18   Q.      WHAT IS YOUR OPINION OF ROUTE "CCG" IN COMPARISON TO

19           ROUTE 894?

20   A.               In its more basic element, Route "CCG", or Route Cherokee Creek

21           G, is 9.02 miles longer than Alternative Route 894. I used the Applicant's

22           Table 7-2 in Appendix E to the EA (Attachment 1 of the Application), which

23           lists their quantifications by criterion for each of the Alternative Route.


     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349 and PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                                     Page 9
     Cross-rebuttal Testimony of Jason E. Buntz
     On behalf of Colorado River Alliance Intervenors - May 22,2026
  1           Route "CCG" has a total length of 232.19 miles. Alternative Route 894 is

 2           223.17 miles in length or 9.02 miles shorter than Route "CCG".

 3   Q.      DOES MS. REINECKE REFLECT THE ESTIMATED COST OF ROUTE

 4           "CCG" IN HER DIRECT TESTIMONY?

 5   A.               No, Ms. Reinecke does not provide an estimate of the transmission

 6           line cost of Route "CCG" in her direct testimony. The Applicants estimated

 7           the transmission line cost for Route Cherokee Creek G at $1,754,606,644,

 8           or $73,687,644 more than Alternative Route 894, which has an estimated

 9           cost of $1,680,919,000.

10   Q.      HOW MANY HABITABLE STRUCTURES DOES ROUTE "CCG" HAVE

11           WITHIN 500 FEET OF ITS CENTERLINE?

12   A.               In Ms. Reinecke's direct testimony (page 12, line 27) she indicates

13           that Route "CCG" would have 105 habitable structures within 500 feet of

14           its centerline, or 20 more than Alternative Route 894 which has 85.

15   Q.      DOES MS. REINECKE PROVIDE COMPARISONS OF ROUTE "CCG"

16           AND ROUTE 894 WITH RESPECT TO THE GOLDEN-CHEEKED

17           WARBLER?

18   A.               Yes. Ms. Reinecke quantified potential impacts to what she labels

19           as Golden-cheeked Warbler habitat using Mueller et al 2022.

20   Q.      COULD YOU DESCRIBE MUELLER ET AL 2022?

21   A.               Certainly. James Mueller and his colleagues conducted a study of

22           Golden-cheeked Warblers that was published in 2022 in the Journal of

23           Wildlife Management. Mueller's study resulted in a predictive model of


     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349 and PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                                      Page 10
     Cross-rebuttal Testimony of Jason E. Buntz
     On behalf of Colorado River Alliance Intervenors - May 22,2026
  1           high, medium, and low densities of male warblers based on a remote

 2           sensing evaluation of the composition of Ashe juniper and broadleaf tree

 3           cover across a 67,861-sqaure kilometer area in 35 Texas counties, some

 4           of which overlap with the Study Area in this docket. Mueller also

 5           conducted random sampling to survey for male warblers within the

 6           modeled habitat areas. Within the Study Area for the Bell County East to

 7           Big Hill transmission line project, the highest densities predicted by

 8           Mueller tend to be found along the Colorado River and around Lake

 9           Buchanan. The publicly available version of Mueller's model was released

10           in 2025.

11   Q.      DO YOU AGREE WITH MS. REINECKE'S OPINION THAT ROUTE

12           "CCG" CROSSES FEWER MILES OF GOLDEN-CHEEKED WARBLER

13           HABITAT THAN ROUTE 894?

14   A.               I'll leave the opinions on this issue of "habitat" to Dr. Morrison's

15           direct testimony on behalf of the Colorado River Alliance, as he confirmed

16           the presence of Golden-cheeked Warblers along the path of Link J31, a

17           component of RFI Route Cherokee Creek G and Ms. Reinecke's Route

18           "CCG". l will say, though, that Mueller provides a model of predicted

19           habitat densities and not a spatial dataset of known warbler habitat

20           surveyed in the field. Even so, the Applicants' Environmental Assessment,

21           Table 7-2, suggests that Route "CCG" crosses about .02 miles of "known

22           habitat of federally listed endangered or threatened species," while Route

23           894 crosses .09 miles. More importantly, Dr. Morrison has proven the


     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349 and PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                                       Page 11
     Cross-rebuttal Testimony of Jason E. Buntz
     On behalf of Colorado River Alliance Intervenors - May 22,2026
  1           presence of Golden-cheeked Warblers along the path of Link J31, a

 2           component of RFI Route "CCG."

 3   Q.      MS. REINECKE OFFERS HER OPINION IN HER DIRECT TESTIMONY

 4           THAT LINK J31 IS A "SUPERIOR OPTION" FOR CROSSING THE

 5           COLORADO RIVER? DO YOU AGREE WITH THIS OPINION?

 6   A.               This one, no. I do not. As I stated earlier in my response to Mr.

 7           Brewer's testimony, Dr. Morrison found multiple instances of Golden-

 8           cheeked Warblers in the area proposed for Link J31 proximate to the

 9           Colorado River on his May 6, 2026, visit to the Colorado River Alliance's

10           properties.

11                    In measuring the lengths in miles of Links J22 and J31 across

12           areas shown as warbler habitat in Mueller's model, I come up with 1.9

13           miles for Link J22 and 5.9 miles for Link J31. Furthermore, just in looking

14           at the Mueller model that Ms. Reinecke uses to derive her calculation of

15           length of miles of route "CCG" across Golden-cheeked Warbler habitat, it

16           is clear to me that Link J31 crosses more area modeled by Mueller than

17           does Link J22. In fact, although the Applicants do not cite the Mueller

18           study in the EA , the image below leaves me with the distinct impression

19           that Link J22 was routed to the extent practicable to avoid and minimize
20           intersecting areas along the Colorado River modeled by Mueller as

21           Golden -checked Warbler habitat . \f we are just talking Links , without the

22           context of an overall end-to-end route, the superior option for crossing the

23           Colorado River would be along Link U3, in my opinion.

                                                            IV. SUMMARY
N




            Q.      FOLLOWING YOUR REVIEW OF THE DIRECT TESTIMONIES OF MR.
Oo




                    BREWER AND MS. REINECKE, HAS YOUR OPINION CHANGED WITH

                    RESPECT TO ALTERNATIVE ROUTE 894 AS BEST MEETING THE
CD




                    CRITERIA                    UNDER     PURA §    37.056(c) AND   PUC SUBST.               R.         §

                    25.101(b)(3)(B)?

            A.                    No, it has not. I still believe the selection by Oncor/LCRA TSC of

                    Route 894 as the route that best balances the PURA § 37.056(c)(4) and

                    PUC SuBsT. R. § 25.101(b)(3)(B) criteria is reasonable and well supported

                    by the environmental information presented in the Application.

            Q.      DOES THAT CONCLUDE YOUR CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY?

            A.                    Yes, it does.
